bullets.title: META: $35B equity raise + $60B ATM planned; Hedgeye maintains Top Long on core ad strength
bullets.body: META priced a 40M-share secondary at $625 ($22.5B common via forward sales + $12.5B mandatory convertible preferred) and plans up to $60B Class C ATM in 1Q27+, covering ~half of its $180–220B total funding need through 2028. Full $95B equity equals ~148M shares (5.7% dilution); 2028 EPS ~1% lower vs debt alternative. Hedgeye keeps META as Top Long Idea, arguing core advertising generates ~$111B cash operating profit 2026–2028 and carries the investment thesis despite $40B in new AI/cloud costs. AMD separately announced a $1B equity investment in META and confirmed EPYC processors power Meta's Muse AI agent.

bullets.title: AVGO: $63B Anthropic chip financing deal with $45B residual value guarantee; DA Davidson upgrade
bullets.body: Broadcom arranged a $63B financing vehicle for Anthropic's CY27 chip purchases, providing a $45B residual value guarantee (total RSV exposure now $74B including June CY26 tranche). AVGO shares rose +3.3% pre-market on the deal plus a DA Davidson upgrade. Wolfe Research notes the deal demonstrates AI chip financing models are viable for CY27/28 capex, though risk remains if compute capacity becomes overbuilt.

bullets.title: Anthropic S-1: $16.3B H1'26 revenue (+1,400% YoY); $750B+ compute commitments to AMZN/GOOGL/AVGO
bullets.body: Anthropic's S-1 discloses H1'26 revenue of $16.3B with adjusted net income of $2.7B (vs -$1.7B YoY loss); 11,900+ enterprise customers spending $100K+. The company has committed $110B to AMZN through 2036, $114.5B to GOOGL through 2033, plus $161.2B to Broadcom and $120.5B to SpaceX.AI. Analysts see compute infrastructure beneficiaries (CRWV, NBIS) and cybersecurity platforms (DDOG, CRWD) as key read-throughs; 22V notes customer concentration falling sharply (top-5 share dropped from ~36% to ~21% of revenue Q1–Q3'26).

bullets.title: AMZN: Hedgeye initiates long with $359 PT (+30%) on AWS acceleration to 41% in Q4
bullets.body: Hedgeye adds AMZN as Top Idea Long with $359 PT (vs $250 current, $15 bear case downside) over 12-15 months. AWS growth accelerating to 38.1% in Q3 and 41.0% in Q4 vs. Street's flat 37% consensus; AWS backlog at $496B. Q3 headline deceleration already priced in from Prime Day shift; Q4 re-accelerates to +17.8% sales growth. Citi buyside checks expect AWS ~43% Q3 with NA Retail inline; Alexa for Shopping (300M+ users) showing 48% higher conversion and 21% higher spend vs prior version.

bullets.title: MSFT: F1Q27 preview — Azure +44.3% consensus; buyout of 60K employees (27% of workforce) underway
bullets.body: Street consensus for F1Q27: $90.6B revenue, Azure +44.3% growth (mgmt guided +45% cc), $4.71 EPS. Citi buyside expects Azure +47%+ cc with F2Q guide at similar level. MSFT is offering ~60K voluntary buyouts to maintain margins amid AI capex pressure; Nadella cited inference demand materially stronger than expected. Key investor focus: capex clarity for 2028-2029 and Copilot monetization ramp.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Citi buyside expects 3Q Search ~14.5%, YouTube +12.5%, Cloud revs 100%+; Hedgeye outright short
bullets.body: Citi's buyside channel checks expect strong GOOGL 3Q results: Search ~14.5%, YouTube +12.5%, Cloud revenues >100% YoY. MS notes GOOGL down 6% in 3Q earnings season and trading at 21x '27 EPS (14% below TTM average multiple). Hedgeye flags GOOGL as an outright short with bearish TREND signal.

bullets.title: RCL: Q3 +$6.57 EPS beat; FY26 raised to $17.85-17.95; 2027 bookings at historic highs, $20 handle intact
bullets.body: RCL reported Q3 adj. EPS $6.57 vs guidance $6.26-6.36; net yields +0.6% vs flat guide, driven by close-in Europe/Caribbean demand. FY26 EPS raised to $17.85-17.95 (+14% YoY). 2027 booking volumes up high-teens at higher rates; booked position ahead of historical levels. Sandals/Beaches JV closing early 2027. JPM raises FY27 EPS to $20.49 with $394 PT (OW); UBS maintains Buy at $367 PT. Stock +5.3% pre-market; CCL +2.4% sympathy.

bullets.title: GLW: Q3 beat, Q4 guided +19% revenue growth; AI optical demand accelerating toward $40B sales by 2030
bullets.body: Corning Q3 core EPS $0.91 vs $0.88 est; revenue $5.08B vs $5.03B. Q4 guidance: EPS $0.96-1.00 (36% YoY growth), revenue $5.2-5.3B. AI-related optical demand described as very strong with customers pressing for more capacity; optical scale-up acceleration begins 2028. Springboard plan targets $30B annualized run rate by end 2028 and $40B by end 2030 (19% CAGR 2027-2030). Wolfe hosting 15-min callback webcast today at 11:45am ET.

bullets.title: AXON/MSI: MS upgrades AXON on Body 5 launch; MSI Command Center approaching $1B run rate
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgrades AXON, viewing the recent selloff as a buying opportunity at ~1.3x FY27 PEG vs. 1.7-2x for large-cap software peers. AXON Body 5 (launching early 2027) adds 4K resolution, ~20% longer battery life, and enhanced AI processing; the ~$199/officer/month AI Era Plan upsell represents ~$12K over five-year contracts. MSI Command Center grew ~20% in H1'26, approaching $1B annual run rate; MSI Hyper AI agent achieved 71% deflection rate for non-emergency calls at San Diego County Sheriff's Office.

bullets.title: NOW: Q3 earnings preview — $4.09B revenue consensus; AI ACV momentum vs. organic cRPO deceleration key debate
bullets.body: ServiceNow Q3 consensus: $4.09B revenue ($3.98B subscription), $1.02 EPS, cRPO guidance +19.5% YoY, operating margin ~31%. NOW has beaten revenue 17 of last 20 quarters; options imply ~10.2% move. Bulls cite AI ACV momentum and Federal/Security deals; bears flag organic cRPO deceleration and Microsoft/AI-native competition. Stock up 65.7% since late July vs S&P +2.4%.

bullets.title: FTNT: F3Q26 earnings tomorrow; Street expects slight revenue/margin/EPS beats, focus on FY27 outlook
bullets.body: Fortinet reports F3Q26 on Oct 28. Street expects revenue $2,064M (vs $2,055M guidance midpoint), gross margin 80.1% (+10bps vs guide), operating margin 36.2% (+20bps vs guide), EPS $0.86 vs $0.85 guide. Key investor focus: product vs. service revenue mix, SASE/Firewall momentum, AI Infrastructure & OT security trends, and FY27 demand durability commentary.

bullets.title: SHOP: Citi raises PT to $216; models +34.5% Q3 revenue growth ~300bps above Street
bullets.body: Citi models Shopify Q3 revenue growth of +34.5% YoY (~300bps above Street consensus), with Merchant Solutions +38%. PT raised to $216. MS notes investor focus for upcoming print will be on 4Q guidance, ROI on AI spend, and AI tool monetization; bar has been raised given recent stock strength.

bullets.title: CRWV: Oppenheimer maintains Outperform $150 PT; $83B asset coverage vs $42B debt, 3Q beat expected
bullets.body: Oppenheimer argues CoreWeave's credit market selloff overstates equity risk: ~$83B recoverable assets cover ~$42B pro forma debt in liquidation, and CoreWeave can generate $9-16B annual FCFF by pausing capex in 2027-2028. A100 deal implies nine-year server life vs six-year depreciation. 3Q26 beat expected with modest raise to ~160% YoY full-year revenue growth; CRWV viewed as best-positioned full-software-stack player as compute supply/demand balances.

bullets.title: EQIX: MS names new Top Pick on 49GW global data center capacity shortfall by 2028
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's new data center capacity model estimates global IT demand vs. supply shortfall of 49GW by 2028 (43GW US-only). EQIX named as new Top Pick for colocation advantage — smaller facilities and critical functionality enable performance amid cost inflation and permitting delays. Colocation providers expected to lose only ~3 percentage points of market share to hyperscalers by 2030.

bullets.title: VZ: Q3 postpaid phone adds 406K (+104% vs 199K consensus); FY26 FCF raised ~12% YoY; SpaceX overhang caps upside
bullets.body: Verizon Q3 EPS $1.31 beat by $0.04; retail postpaid phone net adds 406K vs 199K consensus — best in a decade. FY26 EPS raised to $5.04-5.06, postpaid phone net adds raised to 1.1M-1.2M vs prior 750K-1.0M, FCF guidance raised to ~12% growth YoY. AWS AI Connect deal valued at $2B+. TD Cowen cut PT to $55 from $56 citing prolonged SpaceX/Starlink overhang; KeyBanc believes AI Connect barely visible in revenue profile yet.

bullets.title: FWONK/TKO: GS flags FWONK at all-time low EV/EBITDA multiples; Citizens reiterates Outperform on both
bullets.body: Goldman highlights FWONK trading at all-time low forward EV/EBITDA multiples with attractive 2027 setup on easing comps, with a potential ~$40M / ~3% FY2026 OIBDA downside risk from canceled F1 events in 4Q. Citizens maintains Market Outperform on both FWONK and TKO, citing resilient live sports demand with healthy attendance and gate trends for F1 and UFC/WWE events even amid consumer spending pressure.

bullets.title: DELL/HPE/SMCI: Goldman rates DELL and HPE Buy, SMCI Sell; hardware analyst hosting NYC meetings Nov 10
bullets.body: Goldman hardware analyst Kat Murphy is hosting investor meetings in New York on November 10 ahead of earnings season with ratings of Buy on DELL, Buy on HPE, and Sell on SMCI.

bullets.title: CLS: Raises 2027 revenue and OPM guidance; first positive 2028 customer demand commentary; FCF guided -23%
bullets.body: Celestica raised its 2027 revenue and operating margin guidance ahead of expectations and provided its first bullish commentary on 2028 customer demand. However, 2026 FCF guidance was lowered 23% to $460M. JPM notes AWS Trainium 3 liquid-cooled project delayed two months due to downstream ramp hiccups, which could affect near-term CLS volumes.

bullets.title: HUBS: UBS downgrade drives -3.4% pre-market decline
bullets.body: HubSpot fell 3.4% in pre-market trading following a UBS downgrade. No additional PT or thesis detail provided in the items, but the move is notable heading into earnings season for software names.

bullets.title: ARM/AMD/INTC: Wolfe semiconductor webcast Oct 30 to cover INTC this week and AMD/ARM next week
bullets.body: Wolfe Research analyst Chris Caso is hosting a semiconductor webcast on October 30 covering this week's INTC earnings and next week's AMD and ARM results, focused on semis and semiconductor capital equipment trends.
